question_text: What important fact did Millikan's experiment establish?

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students, physics section, Ch.12 (printed p.43); the book prints no exam-year citations for this chapter. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked physically: Millikan's photoelectric experiment (1916) measured stopping potential against frequency for alkali metals; the straight V₀–ν line verified Einstein's photoelectric equation, its slope h/e gave Planck's constant in close agreement with the accepted value, and this led to the acceptance of the photon picture of radiation — the book's account is correct.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter · 2 marks

steps.label: Verified Einstein's equation
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the equation being verified — Einstein's photoelectric equation.
steps.why: Millikan measured the stopping potential at many frequencies and found the straight V₀–ν line that Einstein's equation predicts, so the equation passed a direct experimental test.
common_mistakes: Answering with the oil-drop experiment. That one measured the electron's charge; this question is about his photoelectric experiment.
Saying he discovered the photoelectric effect. He tested Einstein's equation for it.

recall.must_convey: That Millikan's experiment verified Einstein's photoelectric equation.

steps.label: Measured Planck's constant
steps.mark_note: Value of h, photon picture accepted
lines: The same measurements determined the value of
Planck's constant h. This result led to the
acceptance of the photon picture of radiation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two outcomes: the value of h, and the photon picture accepted.
steps.why: In Einstein's equation eV₀ = hν − W₀ the slope of the V₀–ν line is h/e. Measuring that slope gave h itself, and a wave picture of light offers no such line at all.
common_mistakes: Stopping at verified the equation. The measured value of Planck's constant is the second half of the answer.
Writing that he measured the work function. The constant the experiment is known for is h.

recall.must_convey: That the experiment determined Planck's constant and led to acceptance of the photon picture of radiation.

steps.memory_tip: Two prizes from one line: the equation checked, and h read off its slope.

insider_note: Say both facts: the equation verified AND Planck's constant measured — most answers stop at the first and lose the second mark.
